paper_name: Resource Sharing in Global Fixed-Priority Preemptive Multiprocessor Scheduling
paper_description: Develops a novel resource-sharing protocol P-PCP and corresponding schedulability tests for global fixed-priority preemptive multiprocessor scheduling of constrained-deadline sporadic tasks with non-nested resource sharing, along with the first schedulability analysis for PIP in this setting, demonstrating efficiency under reasonable priority assignments.

formal_description.statement: Each sporadic task tau_i (1 <= i <= n) is characterized as (T_i, C_i, D_i), where T_i denotes the minimum inter-arrival time, C_i the worst-case execution time, and D_i the relative deadline. Each job of task tau_i requires C_i units of processing capacity within D_i time units from its release, supplied sequentially.
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the parameters for modeling real-time tasks in the system

informal_sketch.intuition: Tasks generate jobs sporadically with guaranteed minimum separation, each needing a fixed amount of sequential CPU time to meet a deadline relative to release.
steps: For each task tau_i, specify T_i as min time between job releases
Specify C_i as max execution needed per job
Specify D_i as deadline from job release
Ensure jobs do not overlap in execution on multiple cores
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
class Task:
    def __init__(self, i, T, C, D):
        self.i = i  # task index
        self.T = T  # period/inter-arrival
        self.C = C  # execution time
        self.D = D  # deadline

task_set = [Task(i, T_i, C_i, D_i) for i in range(1, n+1)]
key_insights: Models uncertainty in arrivals via minimum separation
Sequential execution prevents parallelism within a job

variables.T_i: minimum inter-arrival time of task tau_i

formal_description.conclusion: Tasks have deadlines no later than their minimum inter-arrival times

informal_sketch.intuition: Deadlines arrive at least as frequently as new jobs, ensuring no implicit overlap in requirements.
steps: Check for every task if deadline D_i <= inter-arrival T_i
This bounds the density of demand from each task
key_insights: Prevents backlog accumulation by aligning deadlines with arrivals

formal_description.statement: A job J of task tau_i is directly blocked at time t on request for resource R_k if: (1) J is one of the m highest effective-priority jobs with remaining execution; (2) R_k is locked by a job with lower base-priority than J; (3) J's request for R_k is ungranted until t.
formal_description.conclusion: Defines priority inversion blocking excluding higher-priority holders

informal_sketch.intuition: Blocking occurs only from lower-priority jobs holding needed resources, when the blocked job would otherwise run on an available processor.
steps: Check if J has top-m effective priority at t
Verify R_k held by lower base-priority job
Confirm request pending and unfulfilled
key_insights: Excludes natural preemption by higher priorities

formal_description.statement: N_l(t, x) = floor( (t - x + D_l) / T_l ); W_l(t, x) = x * N_l(t, x) + min(x, t - x + D_l - T_l * N_l(t, x)) for t >= 0, else 0.

variables.N_l: number of jobs of tau_l with x relevant units in interval t
variables.W_l: total workload of tau_l considering x relevant units in interval t

formal_description.conclusion: Bounds the maximum execution from a task in a time interval, prioritizing relevant portions

informal_sketch.intuition: Counts how many full 'relevant' executions fit in the interval, plus partial for carry-in, to maximize overlap.
steps: Compute number of full jobs: floor( (t - x + D_l)/T_l )
Add partial carry-in: min(x, remainder after full jobs)
Scale by x for relevant part
key_insights: Relevant x allows focusing on resource-critical parts

formal_description.statement: A priority-assignment is reasonable if D_i <= D_j for every pair (tau_i, tau_j) such that tau_i and tau_j are among the n - m lowest base-priority tasks and tau_i has higher base-priority than tau_j.
formal_description.conclusion: Higher priority among low-priority tasks have earlier or equal deadlines, including DM, RM-US(X), DM-US(X)

informal_sketch.intuition: Among tasks that might not always run immediately, tighter deadlines get higher priority to prevent excessive interference.
steps: Identify the n - m lowest priority tasks
For each pair where tau_i > tau_j (higher base prio), check D_i <= D_j
Ensures reasonable ordering for analysis
key_insights: Reduces multi-interference from single low-prio job to at most 2 per resource

formal_description.statement: For reasonable priority-assignment, I_lpi = sum_{l > i} sum_{x: (R_x in RS_l and |R_x| < i)} 2 * CT_l_x / m

variables.I_lpi: lower priority interference bound for tau_i
variables.|R_x|: highest base priority accessing R_x (lowest index)
variables.CT_l_x: total usage of R_x by job of tau_l

formal_description.conclusion: Limits interference from each lower-priority task to at most two resource holdings per shared resource

informal_sketch.intuition: Under reasonable priorities, response time bounds ensure low-prio jobs don't overlap more than twice with higher ones per resource.
steps: Assume RT_i <= D_i for schedulability
For each lower tau_l, D_i <= D_l <= T_l implies RT_i <= T_l
Thus W_l(RT_i, CT_l_x) <= 2 * CT_l_x
Sum over relevant resources and tasks, divide by m for parallelism
key_insights: RT_i <= T_l caps job count to 2
Enables tighter bounds than general case

formal_description.statement: At every time instant and for each task tau_i, POPUP_i <= alpha_i

variables.POPUP_i: number of lower base-prio jobs with pseudo effective-prio > i

assumptions: P-PCP protocol with decreasing alphas: alpha_1 >= ... >= alpha_n >= 0
formal_description.conclusion: P-PCP invariant bounds concurrent low-prio high-pseudo-prio jobs

informal_sketch.intuition: Protocol suspends requests to cap low-prio jobs that could elevate to block higher ones.
steps: Assume violation at t, trace back to last grant at t_f
At t_f-, POPUP_i >= alpha_i, but grant should have checked HPR_z + POPUP_z >= alpha_z for granter z > i
Contradiction since alpha_z <= alpha_i and HPR_z + POPUP_z >= alpha_i
key_insights: Proof by contradiction on grant events

formal_description.statement: For PIP, if i <= m then RT_i = C_i + DB_i + I_hp_ds(RT_i); else RT_i = C_i + DB_i + I_hp_ds(RT_i) + I_hp_os(RT_i) + I_hp_ns(RT_i) + I_lp_i; where terms from Eqs (6)-(10).

variables.RT_i: response time upper bound for tau_i
variables.I_hp_ds: higher prio direct shared resource interference (Eq 7)

assumptions: Global fixed-prio preemptive on m procs
formal_description.conclusion: Provides response-time bound; schedulable if forall i, RT_i <= D_i

informal_sketch.intuition: Accounts for self-execution, blocking/wait for resources, and higher effective-prio interference, divided by m for parallelism; high-prio tasks avoid low-prio interference.
steps: Initialize RT_i = C_i
Add blocking/wait: DB_i + I_hp_ds(RT_i)
If i > m, add remaining higher interferences and low-prio I_lp_i
Solve fixed-point iteratively since recursive
Check RT_i <= D_i for all i
key_insights: For top-m tasks, no low-prio interference due to processor slack

formal_description.statement: For P-PCP, RT_i = C_i + DB_i + SUS_i + I_hp_ds(RT_i) + I_hp_os(RT_i) + I_hp_ns(RT_i) + I_lp_i; where SUS_i from (14), I_hp_os from (15), I_lp_i from (16) if reasonable and D= T else (10).

variables.RT_i: response time upper bound for tau_i

assumptions: Constrained deadline, D_i = T_i for tight bound
Reasonable priority optional for tighter I_lp_i
formal_description.conclusion: Extends PIP bound with suspension; schedulable if forall i, RT_i <= D_i

informal_sketch.intuition: Adds suspension from protocol invariants to PIP terms; tunes alpha_i to trade suspension for reduced low-prio interference.
steps: Compute base as in Theorem 1: C_i + DB_i + interferences
Add SUS_i: sum over requests N_i_k * sum top-alpha_i other C_l_k
For I_hp_os: divide higher osr by min(m, alpha_i)
For I_lp_i: hybrid of top-alpha_i full W_l + remainder capped at 2*CT
Fixed-point solve and check <= D_i
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def compute_RT_PPCP(task_set, m, alphas):
    RT = {task.i: task.C for task in task_set}
    converged = False
    while not converged:
        converged = True
        for task_i in task_set:
            i = task_i.i
            db = compute_DB_i(task_i)
            sus = compute_SUS_i(task_i, task_set, alphas[i-1])
            ihp_ds = compute_I_hp_ds(task_i, RT[i])
            ihp_os = compute_I_hp_os_ppcp(task_i, RT[i], m, alphas[i-1])
            ihp_ns = compute_I_hp_ns(task_i, RT[i])
            ilp = compute_I_lpi_ppcp(task_i, task_set, m, alphas[i-1], reasonable=True)
            new_rt = task_i.C + db + sus + ihp_ds + ihp_os + ihp_ns + ilp
            if abs(new_rt - RT[i]) > 1e-6:
                converged = False
            RT[i] = new_rt
    return RT
key_insights: Alpha_i = m often optimal for low prio tasks
Tighter I_lp_i via partial shift in arrivals
